paper_title: Predicting response to enzalutamide and abiraterone in metastatic prostate cancer using whole-omics machine learning
prediction_task: ARSI treatment response prediction in mCRPC from WGS + WTS + clinical data

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Most patients (even in academic centers) do not undergo WGS/WTS. It would be of great practical relevance to study model performance with targeted panel sequencing data as input, ideally in a separate cohort.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Discussed panel sequencing as future work and showed which features are capturable by commercial panels.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Not clear how treatment response to ARSI can be differentiated from overall prognosis. Is the model predicting aggressive disease rather than features specific to ARSI response?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added treatment-specific interaction analysis and discussed prognostic vs predictive biomarkers.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Figure legends too small to be readable. Figure resolution poor. Distribution of variables not shown. No exploration of how validation cohort differs from training cohort.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Improved all figures and added cohort comparison.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Choice of sparse PCA as feature reduction is well-established but not without difficulties. Covariance of features, captured variance for number of components should be shown. Why logistic regression and not other methods?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added PCA variance explained plots and comparison with other classifiers.

reviewer_strengths.text: Answers a potentially critical clinical question. Well-annotated cohorts, state-of-the-art ML approaches, very clear and concise data presentation.
